articles.title: Surrogate, California couple clash in court as newborn fights for life after heart surgery
articles.summary: Nausheen Gilkar told a Dallas court her newborn is suffering after open-heart surgery as the surrogate custody fight with McKenna West intensifies.
articles.body: The critically ill newborn at the center of a bitter surrogate custody fight was placed back on a breathing tube after his condition worsened following open-heart surgery, according to newly filed court documents. The baby is in critical condition and being closely watched at the hospital, intended parents Nausheen Gilkar and Omar Ahmed said in filings obtained by TMZ. The couple said the child suffered possible complications after a Norwood procedure, an operation used to treat his severe heart defect, and had to be re-intubated after his condition declined overnight. SURROGATE SAYS BABY 'RIPPED AWAY' 60 SECONDS AFTER BIRTH AS CUSTODY FIGHT ERUPTS AFTER ABORTION REFUSAL In a Dallas courtroom Tuesday, Gilkar and Ahmed faced surrogate McKenna West as they fought over who should make medical decisions for the newborn. The clash has drawn national attention because West says she refused the California couple’s earlier request to terminate the pregnancy after the baby was diagnosed with a life-threatening heart condition. Gilkar and Ahmed call the baby Rumi. West, an Alaska cardiac nurse, calls him Gabriel and is asking a Texas judge to give her sole conservatorship, which would put medical decision-making in her hands. HHS WARNS TEXAS HOSPITALS AGAINST DENYING LIFE-SAVING CARE TO NEWBORN WITH DISABILITY Gilkar told the court the couple has been at their son’s bedside as he fights through treatment. She said that since surgery, he has struggled to breathe, choked on tubes and needed a blood transfusion, according to court reporting by The Associated Press. "He’s our child," Gilkar said, according to the AP. She accused West of trying to take him away. "She’s trying to take him from us," Gilkar said. Gilkar described the newborn as "the love of our lives" and said, "He’s suffering a lot." NEONATOLOGIST SOUNDS ALARM OVER MASSACHUSETTS ABORTION LAW ALLOWING PROCEDURES UP TO BIRTH: 'VERY DISTURBING' The custody feud began after the baby was diagnosed at about 20 weeks with hypoplastic left heart syndrome, or HLHS. West says Gilkar and Ahmed then asked her to terminate the pregnancy. She refused and later traveled to Texas to give birth, Fox News Digital previously reported. HLHS leaves one side of the heart underdeveloped and disrupts normal blood flow. Without treatment, the condition can be fatal within days or weeks, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. AMERICAN RED CROSS DECLARES NATIONAL BLOOD CRISIS AS TYPE O SUPPLY DROPS TO DANGEROUS LEVELS Budner disputes key parts of West’s account and says the couple did agree to the baby’s treatment. He told Fox News Digital that doctors determined on Aug. 14 that the child was eligible for the Norwood procedure, the first of three open-heart surgeries generally used to treat HLHS. Gilkar and Ahmed consented to the surgery, which was performed Aug. 17, he said. At the time, Budner described the baby’s condition as "critical and complex." BOARD-CERTIFIED OBGYN WARNS NEW MASSACHUSETTS LATE-TERM ABORTION LAW EXPOSES MOTHERS TO DANGER West’s lawyers have argued that the court should make sure the baby continues to receive life-saving care. West told the judge she would abandon her custody request if the court determines the intended parents are committed to that care, according to the AP. Gilkar and Ahmed have asked the court to delay a hearing over the temporary restraining order that gave them custody while the legal fight continues, TMZ reported. TWO FAMILIES SUE NORTH DAKOTA HOSPITAL ON ALLEGATIONS BABIES WERE SWITCHED AT BIRTH The custody battle is only one part of the couple’s broader legal fight with West. Before the baby was born, Gilkar and Ahmed filed counterclaims seeking more than $100,000, alleging West breached their surrogacy agreement and caused them emotional distress. The counterclaims, obtained by TMZ, said the couple paid West $60,000 during the pregnancy under an agreement that addressed termination. West has denied wrongdoing and asked the court to dismiss the claims. DEM GOV MAURA HEALEY SIGNS SWEEPING MASSACHUSETTS BILL ALLOWING ABORTIONS UP TO BIRTH The dispute has only grown more personal since the baby’s Aug. 12 birth. West said in a New York Post opinion piece last week that she had only about a minute with the newborn, while his umbilical cord was still attached, before he was taken away. A court order has since barred her from seeing or holding the baby. On Tuesday, the judge left that order in place and did not immediately decide the larger question of custody or conservatorship, according to the AP. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton secured an emergency court order before the birth directing that medically necessary care not be delayed or obstructed, Fox News Digital previously reported. Paxton’s office also notified two Dallas medical centers of their obligations to provide life-saving treatment. The Associated Press and Fox News Digital's Jasmine Baehr contributed to this report.

articles.title: Malaysia’s Anwar puts non-aligned stance in focus with remarks on Taiwan
articles.summary: Malaysian leader’s comments on the island have prompted discussion about whether the country is leaning towards China.
articles.body:
Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia – Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim’s recent comments about Taiwan have raised questions about whether Malaysia is still committed to its traditional policy of non-alignment and not picking sides between China and the United States.

In an interview with Al Jazeera that aired earlier this month, Anwar stated that he saw Taiwan “as part of China, period”, adding that this was “accepted by all”.

More controversially, when asked whether he would condemn China if it resorted to force in the event that peaceful “reunification” did not work, Anwar said that if a Malaysian state were attempting to break away, he would use force to “protect the sanctity and unity of” Malaysia.

Anwar’s comments were praised by the Chinese government, with a Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesman stressing that Taiwan is “an inalienable part of China’s territory” and that “China must and will be reunited”.

Taiwan’s government condemned the remarks and warned that Anwar’s “one-sided support for China could negatively impact Taiwanese businesses’ confidence in investing in Malaysia”.

Taiwan, the world’s largest chips producer, is a major investor in Malaysia, particularly in the country’s crucial semiconductor industry.

Asked about the issue by local media, Anwar appeared to walk back some of his comments, stressing that Malaysia respected China’s position but favoured a peaceful resolution to tensions in the Taiwan Strait.

Anwar courted headlines again several days after his Al Jazeera interview when he called for the bolstering of Malaysia’s defences in the Bornean state of Sabah.

He pointed to the development of US-backed military facilities in neighbouring Philippines as justification, in part, for increased defence spending.

The Philippine government is in the process of upgrading military facilities on the island of Balabac, 50km (31 miles) from the Malaysian islands of Banggi and Balambangan.

Balabac was recently added to the Enhanced Defence Cooperation Agreement (EDCA) between Washington and Manila, which granted US forces access to designated locations in the Philippines.

Anwar’s comments have bolstered longstanding suspicions among Western commentators that Malaysia is turning against the West and aligning with China, breaking from Malaysia’s traditional policy of non-alignment.

Indeed, Anwar’s remarks come amid China’s growing economic presence in Malaysia, with Beijing now representing Malaysia’s largest trade partner.

Malaysia has also been one of the most enthusiastic recipients of Chinese investment projects, including under China’s Belt and Road Initiative.

Anwar’s seemingly pro-China stance also comes as Malaysia diverges from the West on other geopolitical issues, such as the ongoing conflicts in the Middle East.

Long a firm critic of Israel, Malaysia under Anwar has been especially vocal in its opposition to Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza.

However, some analysts push back against suggestions of Malaysia undergoing a strategic realignment.

Chee Meng Tan, an assistant professor of business economics at the University of Nottingham Malaysia, noted that Malaysia’s recognition of Taiwan as “part of China” dates to the 1974 communiqué that then-Prime Minister Tun Abdul Razak signed with Chinese Premier Zhou Enlai to establish diplomatic relations between their countries.

“What was new was Anwar’s statement on the potential use of force, which the one China policy policy does not explicitly require,” Tan said.

Tan notes that Anwar’s comments should also be seen in the context of his upcoming trip to China in September, as he may be attempting to appease Beijing.

Daniel Loebell, a PhD student at Northwestern University in the US who has studied Chinese investments in Malaysia, suggested that Anwar’s position merely represents a realist understanding of territorial integrity.

“Though this idea of violence against Taiwan is immensely troubling to me, I do not think it differs from Malaysia’s policy at all, as he believes that the PRC attacking Taiwan would amount to attacking a rebel organisation within a single state’s own borders,” Loebell said, using the acronym for the People’s Republic of China.

“As head of the government, Anwar sees recognising one government of China amounting to the PRC government’s exclusive right to a monopoly on the use of force within its borders.”

Anwar’s later comments expressing unease over the US-backed base on Balabac can be viewed as linked to Malaysia’s ongoing dispute with the Philippines over the status of Sabah.

The Philippines has claimed Sabah since the territory joined Malaysia in 1963, a claim Malaysia has consistently rejected.

Manila would reaffirm its claim to Sabah in February this year, maintaining that the Philippines’ Maritime Zones Act 2024 preserved its “existing and valid claims” over part of the state.

In July, the Malaysian government lodged a formal protest with the United Nations over the Philippines’ claim to an extended continental shelf, which Malaysia argued encroached on Sabahan waters.

Tan, the assistant professor, argued that Anwar’s comment on the Balabac military buildup may be “a ‘protect-my-border’ reflex rather than a pro-China gesture”.

Anwar’s call to invest in Sabah’s defences also comes as Malaysia seeks to strengthen its defence posture in Borneo, largely to bolster its claims in the disputed South China Sea, where Malaysia is a claimant state alongside China.

While Malaysia has taken a decidedly less vocal stance on the South China Sea dispute than the Philippines, it has nonetheless maintained strong defence ties with Western powers, partly to quietly balance against China’s aggressive military buildup in the disputed waters.

This is demonstrated in Malaysia’s continued commitment to the Five Powers Defence Arrangements (FPDA), a multilateral security framework that also includes Singapore, Australia, New Zealand, and the United Kingdom.

While not a binding defence treaty, the FPDA commits its members to consult with one another in the event of an armed attack on Malaysia or Singapore. Under the framework, two major exercises are held annually – Bersama Shield and Bersama Lima – involving personnel and assets from member countries.

The FPDA maintains an air defence operations arm with headquarters at a Malaysian Air Force base in Butterworth, Penang, headed by a senior Australian Air Force officer.

Australia also maintains a rifle company at Butterworth and a regular maritime security presence in the region via the deployment of maritime patrol aircraft to Malaysia.

As a central pillar of the FPDA, Malaysia facilitates a Western military presence in the region, which analysts argue provides Malaysia with a quiet deterrent for would-be aggressors.

While Malaysia recognises the benefits of continued defence ties with the West, it also gains from continued Western investment.

As Loebell, the PhD student, noted, Malaysia has “maintained diverse economic relations with many states, and this has kept it from deeply aligning with any major power”.

“The USA still maintains as favourable an economic position as China does,” said Loebell, who doubts that Malaysia is seeking to align more closely with China.

“What’s more, Taiwan’s enterprises continue to invest heavily in Malaysia’s semiconductor industry, and Anwar undoubtedly knows and welcomes this.”

articles.title: U.S. military says it killed four in strike on alleged drug-smuggling boat in the Caribbean
articles.summary: The latest attack brings the number of people who have been killed in boat strikes by the U.S. military to at least 227 in 68 strikes since the Trump administration began targeting those it calls “narcoterrorists” almost a year ago.
articles.body: WASHINGTON — The U.S. military attacked a boat suspected of being used to smuggle drugs in the Caribbean Sea on Tuesday, killing four people, as the Trump administration continues its monthslong campaign against alleged traffickers in Latin America. The latest attack brings the number of people who have been killed in boat strikes by the U.S. military to at least 227 in 68 strikes since the Trump administration began targeting those it calls “narcoterrorists” almost a year ago. As with most of the military’s statements on strikes in the eastern Pacific Ocean and Caribbean Sea, U.S. Southern Command said it targeted the alleged drug traffickers along known smuggling routes. The military did not provide evidence that the vessel was ferrying drugs. A video posted on X showed an image of what appeared to be a moving boat followed by a flash. Tuesday’s strike came just two days after the U.S. military carried out a strike on a vessel in the eastern Pacific Ocean, killing two people accused of trafficking drugs. That action came after a pause of more than two months in the U.S. campaign against alleged smugglers. The Trump administration is pursuing deals with allied nations to extend its offensive to land across multiple Latin American countries. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said during a visit to Panama this month that Colombia, Guatemala and Honduras had agreed to allow the U.S. to carry out joint military operations against criminal groups on their soil. Guatemala denied reaching such a deal. Ecuador launched similar missions with the U.S. in March. President Donald Trump has said the U.S. is in “armed conflict” with cartels in Latin America and has justified the attacks as a necessary escalation to stem the flow of drugs into the United States and fatal overdoses claiming American lives. But his administration has offered little evidence to support its claims of killing smugglers.

articles.title: Mumbai auto drivers learn to refuse rides... in Marathi
articles.summary: MUMBAI: 'No' has got some stiff competition in Mumbai after the mandatory requirement of working knowledge of Marathi has, of late, seen cab and autor.
articles.body: MUMBAI: 'No' has got some stiff competition in Mumbai after the mandatory requirement of working knowledge of Marathi has, of late, seen cab and autorickshaw drivers rushing to polish their language skills. After having picked up basic Marathi at RTO-run language classes, some auto drivers are using their newly acquired vocabulary to rustle up a string of excuses to refuse rides.One auto driver in Kurla has scribbled down what he claims are essential phrases in Marathi to get by. Most of these are different ways to turn down passengers - from "mala jevayla jayche aahe" (I need to eat), "mala lagvi la jayche aahe" (I need to use the restroom) and "mala ghari jaychay" (I need to go home), to "mala gas bharaychay" (I need to refill CNG) and "mala riksha durust karaychi aahe" (I need to repair the auto).The driver's notes aren't entirely dedicated to strategic refusals, though. They include practical phrases such as "hoy, basa" (yes, please sit), "kuthey jaychay?" (where do you want to go?), "to kuthe aahe?" (where is that place?) and "ujvi/davi kade gheu?" (should I take a right/left?). Along with the all-important financial vocabulary of Mumbai's transport ecosystem: "sutte dya" (please give change) and "sutte nahi" (I don't have change).The rush for acquiring Marathi-speaking skills comes as the state has enforced the amended Motor Vehicles Rules that require drivers of all commercial passenger vehicles in the state to possess a working knowledge of the language.However, the fear of a crackdown saw a large-scale protest by a section of non-Marathi-speaking autorickshaw and taxi drivers, who stayed off the roads Monday. As commuters bore the brunt, facing travel disruptions and steep fare hikes, state govt Tuesday sought to reassure transport workers by announcing 161 Marathi language training centres across the state and a dedicated RTO helpline to address complaints of harassment, illegal fines and alleged irregularities during Marathi proficiency checks. Transport minister Pratap Sarnaik said the centres would become operational within the next two to three days.Drivers who fail the on-road tests for Marathi-speaking skills are being given a one-month notice period to learn the language. However, driver unions have sought more time and support for compliance. CM Devendra Fadnavis had said Monday that govt was willing to give more time to learn the language.Sarnaik clarified that drivers would first receive a one-month notice, followed by a three-month suspension period. He added that the agency asked him to notify them in advance if he did make any travel plans.Also Read | â$100,000 reward for raising Khalistani flags before EU leadersâ: FIR filed against Gurpatwant Singh Pannun ahead of Republic DayâI was warned under the terms of a âDuty to Warnâ law in the United States,â Pannun told the Associated Press, referring to a provision that requires US intelligence and law enforcement agencies to alert individuals when they become aware of credible and specific threats involving murder, serious bodily harm or kidnapping.âIâm not afraid of their death threats. Iâm going to continue, even at the cost of a bullet,â Pannun said.His remarks came after he claimed that the RCMP had also warned him by telephone on Tuesday. Neither law enforcement agency, however, disclosed details of the alleged plot or threat.Pannun further stated that Canadian law enforcement officials had issued similar âDuty to Warnâ advisories to Hardeep Singh Nijjar, another Khalistani terrorist and a Canadian citizen, in the weeks leading up to his assassination in Surrey, Canada, in June 2023.Nijjarâs killing had triggered a major diplomatic row between Canada and India after the then-Justin Trudeau government alleged that the Indian government was involved in the assassination. articles.title: As Intelâs CPU market share falls to 31-year low in the market that analysts call 'ugliest segment'
articles.summary: Tech News News: Intelâs share in the x86 CPU market for PCs and servers reportedly fell under 70 percent for the first time ever since the year 1995. According to a r.
articles.body: Intelâs share in the x86 CPU market for PCs and servers reportedly fell under 70 percent for the first time ever since the year 1995. According to a report by Mercury Research, first quoted by CRN, the Intel numbers mark a 31-year low for the semiconductor giant, even as AI spending fueled historic growth for its data center business. Dean McCarron, president of Prescott, Arizona-based CPU-tracking company Mercury Research, confirmed the point about Intelâs 31-year low to CRN in an email following the release of his second-quarter CPU market share report comparing Intel and AMD.Asked to comment, an Intel spokesperson referred CRN to record year-over-year sales growth for its Data Center Group and momentum in its client business unit touted in its latest earnings report as well as a growing number of long-term supply agreements.As per the Mercury report, Intelâs overall x86 CPU market share fell 6.5 points year over year and dropped by under 1 point sequentially to 69.3 percent as AMDâs position grew just as much to 30.7 percent, a new record for the rival, the researcher said.Market share of Intel and AMD in various sub-segments now stands as follows:* Desktop CPU: Intel at 65.1 percent vs. AMD at 34.9 percent* Laptop: Intel at 71.1 percent vs. AMD at 28.9 percentThese figures were based on total CPU shipments for PCs and servers, not including semicustom, embedded and IoT products. If those latter three segments were included, Intelâs share for the second quarter would stand at 65.9 percent, down 4.6 points year over year and down 1.5 points sequentially, against AMDâs 34.1 percent, according to Mercury.One thing that is said to have helped AMD was "better than expected" shipments of the companyâs system-on-chips for gaming consoles. Unlike AMD, Intel does not have a big console business for its chips.Coming back, in the PC market, AMDâs share grew by 6.4 percent year-over-year to a record 30.3 percent against Intelâs 69.7 percent. What also needs to be noted here is that total desktop PC shipments declined by 20 percent year-over-year in the second quarter.How the 'ugliest' segment of the market faredOverall, the report describes the desktop X86 CPU market as "ugly." Hit by limited availability of graphics cards and high prices of components like motherboards, memory modules, and SSDs, the desktop CPU market was particularly weak in the second quarter and shrunk by over 20% year-on-year (YoY) as well as quarter-over-quarter (QoQ) due to seasonality. According to Mercury Research, both AMD and Intel suffered significant annual shipment declines, but AMD all in all held up better.Get the latest technology news and updates. Download the TOI App.

articles.title: US Court to pharma giant Guardant Health: You willfully infringed patents for cancer-testing; asked to pay $245 million to University of Washington
articles.summary: Tech News News: A federal judge has finalized a judgment ordering pharma giant Guardant Health to pay more than $245 million to Seattle-based biotech startup TwinStra.
articles.body: A federal judge has finalized a judgment ordering pharma giant Guardant Health to pay more than $245 million to Seattle-based biotech startup TwinStrand Biosciences and the University of Washington for willfully infringing on patented DNA sequencing technology. The final order, entered in the U.S. District Court for the District of Delaware, formalizes an initial November 2023 jury verdict against Guardant. In addition to the upfront payout, the ruling guarantees TwinStrand and the university an ongoing 6% royalty on covered Guardant products through the expiration of the patents in March 2033.TwinStrand was spun out of the University of Washington in 2015 to commercialize the platform. Among its co-founders is molecular biologist and oncologist Dr Jesse Salkâgrandson of polio vaccine developer Jonas Salkâwho served as CEO until 2022 and now co-leads cancer diagnostics firm CytoTerra. Since its founding, TwinStrand has drawn backing from prominent venture firms, including Madrona Venture Group, Soleus Capital, and Section 32, the latter of which led a $50 million Series B round in 2021.The dispute centers on 'Duplex Sequencing,' a breakthrough method developed at the University of Washington that increases the accuracy of next-generation DNA sequencing by more than 10,000-fold. By eliminating standard sequencing errors, the technology allows clinicians and researchers to detect ultra-rare genetic mutations critical for early cancer detection and monitoring.The jury found that Guardant incorporated this proprietary technology without a license across 11 diagnostic products and services, including its flagship Guardant360, Guardant Reveal, and Guardant Shield tests. Following the verdict, the Delaware court denied Guardant's motions to overturn the decision or grant a new trial."Duplex Sequencing solved an accuracy problem the sequencing field had worked on for years, and this judgment affirms the juryâs finding that Guardant Health built products on that invention without a license," said Chad Waite, chair of TwinStrandâs board of directors. "We remained steadfast in our conviction that the facts would prevail, and they have."The $245.2 million total includes: $83.4 million in original jury-awarded damages for infringement through June 2023; $119.4 million in accrued royalties; $22.9 million in interest; and $19.5 million in supplemental damages.Guardant Health says that it will appealGuardant Health announced that it will appeal the final judgment from the U.S. District Court for the District of Delaware related to intellectual property claims brought against Guardant by TwinStrand Biosciences, Inc. and University of Washington, with execution of the final judgment and collection of potential royalties stayed pending appeal.âWe strongly disagree with this decision and will promptly be appealing for its overturn,â said John Saia, Guardant Health Chief Legal Officer. âWe have full faith in the strengths and merits of Guardantâs intellectual property and R&D and are confident we will ultimately prevail on appeal.âImportantly, the order published regarding the scope of royalties expressly defined the products included as those that existed at the time of the trial in 2023, many of which have been discontinued or significantly upgraded. Based on Guardantâs updated technology the current versions of Guardant Reveal and Shield are excluded from the order and potential royalties. In addition, the company has validated design improvements to Guardant360 and related services that would exclude impact of the potential ongoing royalties in the decision.Guardant remains confident that it did not infringe the asserted patents. Both TwinStrand patents have been preliminarily invalidated in the companyâs ongoing challenges before the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office. Separately, Guardant is pursuing appeals before the US Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit.Get the latest technology news and updates. Download the TOI App.

articles.title: âThey opposed Ambedkarâs Constitution, wanted Manusmritiâ: Owaisi targets RSS, BJP
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: AIMIM president Asaduddin Owaisi has launched a sharp attack on the RSS and BJP over the Manusmriti, questioning their commitment to the In.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: AIMIM president Asaduddin Owaisi has launched a sharp attack on the RSS and BJP over the Manusmriti, questioning their commitment to the Indian Constitution. He accused them of historically favouring the ancient text over the document adopted by the country.Owaisi made the remarks during his address at the Jalsa-e-Rahmatul-lil-Alameen at Darussalam .n Hyderabad on the occasion of the 1501st Eid Milad-un-Nabi. He targeted the RSS over its reported opposition to the Constitution drafted by Dr BR Ambedkar and contrasted the organisation's position with that of Muslim freedom fighters during British rule."I am asking those associated with the RSS about Manusmriti. Is it not true that on November 26, 1949, we adopted the Constitution? Yet, four days later, on November 30, a mouthpiece of the RSS published a complaint against it, stating that it wasn't a constitution at all and that it should have been the Manusmriti. They had issues with the Constitution drafted by Babasaheb Ambedkar," Owaisi said.The AIMIM chief also attacked Hindutva ideologue VD Savarkar, referring to his correspondence with the British during his imprisonment in the Andaman cellular jail."Savarkar was in support of Manusmriti. While he was in Andaman jail, he was writing letters to the British, saying, 'I am with you, please release me.' But what were we doing? Allama Fazl-e-Haq Khairabadi was also in jail; he endured hardships but never wrote a 'love letter' to the British. Instead, he issued a fatwa for Jihad against them. Even today, his grave stands in the Andaman as a testament," he asserted.Owaisi further sought to highlight the role of Muslim figures in India's freedom struggle. He claimed that the first prisoner sent to the Andaman Islands was Maulvi Alauddin, the Imam of Hyderabad's Mecca Masjid."Listen, BJP and RSS people, who was the first prisoner in Andaman? It was not your father, grandfather, or ancestor. It was Hyderabad's Maulvi Alauddin, the Imam of Mecca Masjid. He was the first prisoner," Owaisi told the gathering.His remarks come amid an intensifying political confrontation between the BJP and Congress over the Manusmriti and its place in India's social and constitutional discourse.The BJP has recently targeted Congress leader and Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi over his criticism of the Manusmriti. It accused Rahul of making statements that undermine India's traditions, cultural heritage and democratic institutions. Several BJP leaders, including chief ministers, have alleged that Rahul Gandhi's remarks sought to "belittle" India's civilisational values.At an event titled 'Chhatron ki Goonj' in Pune, Rahul Gandhi criticised a passage attributed to the Manusmriti concerning women's independence."This is a direct quote from the Manusmriti, and these words are a shame, because these words should never ever have been spoken," Gandhi said after quoting the passage: "In childhood, a female belongs to her father. In youth, she belongs to her husband. When her lord is dead, she belongs to her sons. A woman must never be independent."Rahul also called for an end to patriarchal structures, telling female students that the country needs to "smash the prevailing patriarchy" to achieve genuine empowerment for women.The exchange has brought the Manusmriti back into the centre of a wider political debate over constitutional values, social equality and competing interpretations of India's cultural and political history.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Kinley Rasmus breaks LLWS hits record for a girl, 1 day after notching her second strikeout record
articles.summary: Kinley Rasmus continues to etch her name in the Little League World Series record book.
articles.body:
Kinley Rasmus continued her dominant run at the Little League World Series on Tuesday with another tournament record as her Phenix City, Alabama, team advanced from another elimination game.

A day after tying the total strikeouts records for a girl in the Little League World Series, Rasmus broke the tournament's record for most hits by a girl. She did so with a fifth-inning single that put runners on the corners in a 4-2 win for Phenix City over Tacoma, Washington.

The hit was Rasmus' fifth of the tournament to claim the record as her own. And Phenix City advanced while eliminating Tacoma.

On Monday, Rasmus made LLWS history on the mound — for the second time.

Rasmus struck out six to help lift Phenix City past West Chester, Pennsylvania, 6-5, in their elimination game Monday. The two-way star has compiled 14 total strikeouts in the tournament, which again matched Mo'ne Davis for the most strikeouts by a girl in tournament history.

Rasmus struck out eight in Phenix City's first game at the Little League World Series last week, which also tied a single-game record Davis set in 2014.

And thanks in part to Rasmus, Phenix City rallied out of a five-run hole on Monday night. Rasmus threw more than four scoreless innings after coming in for relief to help spark the rally. It marked the team's second straight elimination win.

Rasmus is the daughter of former MLB pitcher Cory Rasmus and the niece of former MLB outfielder Colby Rasmus . Cory is an assistant coach for Phenix City this summer, and both brothers played on Phenix City's 1999 Little League World Series team.

Rasmus is one of two girls playing in the tournament this year. Carsynn Meyer is playing for Paseo Verde (Nevada). They are among the 25 girls who have competed in the event's 79-year history.

While Phenix City can't lose again and advance, Rasmus has already put herself in elite LLWS company. She's one strikeout away from breaking Davis' record and may have another chance on the mound thanks to Tuesday's win.

Phenix City will next face Great Lakes winner Hamilton, Ohio, on Wednesday in another elimination game.

articles.body: For many Indians, scanning a QR code to pay for a cup of chai or a packet of biscuits barely registers anymore. You scan, pay and move on.But for one French woman visiting India, the sheer number of QR codes she came across was a genuine surprise.In a video shared online, she spoke about how different India's everyday payment culture felt compared with what she was used to in France. She already knew about UPI before coming to India, but she hadn't expected to see it being used so casually for tiny, everyday purchases.A cup of chai? There was a QR code.Street food? Another one.An autorickshaw ride? She could pay digitally.Even when buying a snack worth just Rs 20, a UPI payment was often an option.And that seemed to be the part that really caught her attention.âI really didn't expect thisâWhat surprised her wasn't just seeing UPI in big shops or restaurants. It was how far it had spread into everyday life.She spotted QR codes at roadside stalls, small neighbourhood shops, cafes, rickshaws and other tiny businesses. For her, it was one of those small cultural differences that becomes noticeable only when you're actually living through it.âComing from France, this was one of those little everyday cultural differences that made me think, âWowâ¦ I really didn't expect this,ââ she wrote in the caption accompanying her video.ID@undefined Caption not available.ID@undefined Caption not available.The post quickly got people talking, with many Indians pointing out that this has become such a normal part of daily life that most people don't even think twice about it anymore.One person commented that they hadn't used cash in years, while another pointed out that even a Rs 10 roadside tea can now be paid for through UPI.And that's perhaps what makes India's digital payment story interesting. The same QR code-based system can be found at a tiny food stall as easily as at a large store.UPI has changed everyday paymentsUPI, or Unified Payments Interface, was launched in 2016 by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI). In January 2026, UPI processed 21.70 billion transactions, worth more than Rs 28.33 lakh crore.So while a QR code stuck to a roadside tea stall might look completely ordinary to an Indian customer, it can still be quite a striking sight for someone seeing this payment culture for the first time.For the French visitor, it was a simple observation from her trip. articles.title: US halts visa appointments globally amid Donald Trump's immigration crackdown
articles.summary: US News: The US has paused visa appointments for applicants around the world as the Trump administration launches a global training programme for consular offi.
articles.body: The US has paused visa appointments for applicants around the world as the Trump administration launches a global training programme for consular officers amid its broader immigration crackdown.A US State Department spokesperson said on Tuesday that the department had begun a training initiative at all US embassies and consulates worldwide. Visa appointment schedules will be adjusted to accommodate the training, the spokesperson said, according to Reuters.The State Department did not provide details on the training or specify how long the adjustments would last.It said the programme was aimed at helping consular officers screen applicants who could potentially become dependent on US public benefits and ensure that visa applications are evaluated "comprehensively and consistently".According to a Financial Times report, immigrant visa applicants with scheduled interviews at US embassies and consulates had received emails informing them that their appointments were being rescheduled and that they would be notified of new dates.The development comes as President Donald Trump's administration continues a broad immigration crackdown that has included visa and green-card revocations and the rejection of applications on various grounds, including political opinions and participation in pro-Palestinian protests.Trump has said the crackdown is intended to improve domestic security.Immigration crackdown faces legal challengesThe administration's immigration policies have also faced legal setbacks. A US judge on Friday struck down a policy that suspended the issuance of immigrant visas to applicants from 75 countries, ruling that the measure exceeded secretary of state Marco Rubio's statutory authority.The administration has also moved to tighten restrictions on legal immigration.The US Department of Homeland Security has proposed making permanent a $103,265 fee for new cap-subject H-1B visa petitions, after a previous $100,000 fee imposed by Trump was blocked by a court.The proposed fee would significantly increase the cost for employers hiring foreign workers in specialised fields.The H-1B programme allows US employers to hire foreign workers with specialised training. The programme provides 65,000 visas annually, along with another 20,000 for workers with advanced degrees.Trump's administration has also ordered enhanced vetting of H-1B applicants and proposed changes to the visa selection process that would favour higher-skilled and better-paid workers.Visa revocations add to pressure on applicantsThe administration is separately preparing to revoke the business and tourism visas of potentially up to 200,000 foreigners who have applied for or are currently seeking asylum in the US.The proposed action would cover B1 and B2 visas issued between 2016 and 2026 whose holders have sought or are seeking asylum. The State Department is expected to announce the move in the coming weeks, according to news agency AP.B1 visas are generally issued for business travel, while B2 visas are generally used for tourism, family visits or medical treatment.The administration has also tightened screening requirements for visa applicants, including demands for additional information about their social media histories and, in some cases, expensive visa bonds.The latest pause in appointments therefore comes as the Trump administration continues to review and tighten several aspects of the US immigration and visa system.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Matthew Liberatore Hit Hard as Orioles Humiliate Cardinals Tuesday Night
articles.summary: Tuesday night was an opportunity for the St. Louis Cardinals to rebound from a profoundly disappointing end to the road trip returning home from Philadelphia...
articles.body:
Tuesday night was an opportunity for the St. Louis Cardinals to rebound from a profoundly disappointing end to the road trip returning home from Philadelphia , but would they? Much of that would depend on which version of Matthew Liberatore took the mound for the Cardinals. The answer is not the one most Cardinals fans were hoping for and the end result was appalling. Not to spoil this for you if you didn't see the game, but everyone in Busch Stadium that was not an Oriole's fan should demand their money back.

The game would get off to an auspicious start in the top of the 1st inning when Matthew Liberatore fielded Jackson Holliday 's dribbler on the 1st base side of the mound and fired the ball over Alec Burleson 's head into right field. Pete Alonso followed that with a solid single into left field with Holliday running on the play which gave the Orioles runners at first and third with no outs. Matthew would find a way out of the jam as he got Gunnar Henderson to pop out and then struck out Mayo and Encarnacion-Strand.

The top of the 3rd inning would be similar to the top of the 1st, but the result would be much different. Taveras reached as he beat out an infield hit. Jackson Holliday whistled a single into center which brought up Pete Alonzo who was not fooled by an 88 mph changeup which he sent soaring 435 feet deep into the left field stands for a 3-0 Baltimore lead. Two outs later, Encarnacion-Strand absolutely annihilated a 94 mph four-seam Liberatore fastball 450 feet even deeper into the left field stands for a 4-0 Orioles lead. That's the longest home run in Busch Stadium this season.

The Cardinals would not go away completely silently. Nathan Church waited on a 72 mph curveball from Orioles pitcher Chris Bassett and ripped it 405 feet into the Cardinals bullpen giving St. Louis a run making the score 4-1. That's the lone St. Louis Cardinals highlight, by the way.

That brief moment of St. Louis Cardinals optimism was short-lived. Matthew Liberatore would not survive the 5th inning. Jackson Holliday led off with his third hit of the night followed by another single from Cardinals nemesis Pete Alonzo. Matthew Liberatore then walked Gunnar Henderson to load the bases with no one out. Liberatore's last batter was Mayo who he surrendered a single to making it 5-1 Orioles and even though Matthew was done, Baltimore wasn't done scoring. Liberatore's replacement was Peter Strzelecki who didn't fare much better than his predecessor. He immediately gave up a single to Encarnacion-Strand which plated two more Orioles upping the Baltimore lead to 7-1. Stzelecki did accomplish one good thing during his relief outing. He struck out Basallo and…yeah, that's it. Next he hit Franklin with a pitch, gave up a single to Taveras, a single to Holliday and a double to Alonzo. When the dust settled, it was 12-1 Orioles and by the time the horrific 5th inning was done, Caleb Ferguson was in the game as the designated "you're pitching until you're too tired to pitch for the rest of the game" guy.

As many of the regulars for both teams sat going into the top of the 6th inning, the Orioles decided to score again just for fun when Ferguson gave up back-to-back doubles to Franklin and Beavers. 13-1 Baltimore. Someone please make it stop. Oh, did I say that out loud?

The Cardinals brought in Ryan Fernandez to take care of the Oriole's 7th inning. After Carlos Narvaez hit a double, it's almost like the Orioles had to try hard NOT to score. When Henderson grounded out, he seemed to just stroll to third as if he felt guilty about possibly scoring another run. Fortunately, Fernandez was able to get out of the inning without further humiliation. By contrast, the Orioles starter Chris Bassitt pitched deep into the bottom of the 7th inning when he was finally lifted for Baltimore reliever Cano.

Instead of going into any more details about the nuts and bolts of what happened for the start of the St. Louis Cardinals homestand, I can sum it up in 3 words: THAT. WAS. UGLY.

I'll add just one more thought before calling it a night. Was Matthew Liberatore's performance sub-par? Sure it was, but that's no excuse for what I perceived as an overall lack of energy from the St. Louis Cardinals Tuesday night. The fact that the game completely got out of hand in the 5th inning didn't help, but if they expect fans to fill the stands anytime soon, a better effort isn't just expected. It is demanded. I know it's a long season and we're nearing the end of it, but I'd like to see some resemblance of the young, hungry team we saw during the first couple of months. I started watching Tuesday night's game believing the Cardinals could muster a run to grab the third Wild Card slot. Now? Give me a break. Put a fork into this season. This team is done. I'd love to be proven wrong.

The St. Louis Cardinals will try again against the Baltimore Orioles Wednesday night. Michael McGreevy gets the start for the Cardinals while the Orioles will send Kyle Bradish to the mound. First pitch is scheduled for 6:45pm central time at Busch Stadium while the game broadcast is available via Cardinals.tv.

articles.title: College student fatally shot by police after knocking on wrong door
articles.summary: Glenn Pysher was trying to find his friends when he accidentally knocked on the door of the wrong house. The homeowners called 911 to report an attempted bre...
articles.body:
A 22-year-old college student was fatally shot by police over the weekend after he accidentally knocked on the wrong door of a home in Pennsylvania, and now his parents are demanding answers.

Glenn Pysher, known to his family and friends as Bubba, spent Saturday night celebrating with friends at a local bar in Upper Pottsgrove, Pennsylvania. When the group decided to move the party to a house nearby, Pysher walked there alone and mistakenly knocked on the wrong door.

His mother, Erin Pysher, said she thinks he got "mixed up" because the house is in a wooded area.

The homeowners called 911 to report an attempted break-in. Police arrived early Sunday and found Pysher in the back of the home.

"So he probably was knocking, 'Hey, let me in, where are you at, what are you doing?' And the homeowners thought he was trying to break into the house and called the cops," his mother told CBS News about what she thinks happened.

There, the Montgomery County District Attorney's Office said, an encounter ensued, and Glenn Pysher was shot and killed. The Upper Pottsgrove Police Department has not released any information about the shooting, but said the incident was under investigation.

"At 12:32, we have the call log, he was talking on the phone with his friends," his mother told CBS News. "By 12:35, I believe, the cops had already shown up and shot him."

"No Taser. No nothing. Automatic deadly force," she said, adding that the family hasn't heard anything from the police department. The Montgomery County Detective Bureau did not respond to CBS News' request for comment.

"I just want things to be done right. I want to know the facts," his father, Glenwood Pysher, said.

Erin Pysher says her son loved playing baseball, and he was looking forward to playing at Saint Elizabeth University in Florham Park, New Jersey, where he recently transferred.

"I was going to take him to school and help him set up his dorm room. He was supposed to start classes on Monday," his mother said. "It's unreal. I don't even know how to explain it. It's a feeling of so much sadness in my heart. I can't — it's hard to breathe."

"He was such a good kid," Glenwood Pysher told CBS News. "The community here loved him, and nobody can believe this happened to this young man who wouldn't hurt a fly."

articles.title: Astros Outslug Yankees in 9-7 Victory
articles.summary: The Astros took their first bite out the big apple on Tuesday Night, and it was a big one. Astros 9 Yankees 7. Game one of the post-Dana Brown era had a diff...
articles.body:
The Astros took their first bite out the big apple on Tuesday Night, and it was a big one. Astros 9 Yankees 7.

Game one of the post-Dana Brown era had a different feel with a much-needed result. Call it desperation, call it sharper focus, patience at the plate, or just unwavering effort in erasing deficits. On this night, the Astros fought, and fought again, often manufacturing runs with two outs.

The scoring began in the Top of the 2nd. Yanier Diaz would take an inside first pitch fastball deep. That would be his 9th home run of the season, and the first of two Diaz would hit on the night.

The following frame, the Astros would increase their lead. Jose Altuve worked some two-out magic with a single, advancing on a passed ball and then came around to score on Dalton Varsho's single to left. That made things 2-0.

However, in the bottom of the third the Yankees would immediately place runners on the corners for Cody Bellinger , and with one swing he'd launch a 3-run blast to right field. For Ethan Pecko , it was his first allowed career HR in the majors.

The Astros would tie things up at 3-3 in the 5th. Yordan Alvarez would single to center, Paredes would walk and then once again with two outs Daulton Varsho would come through in the clutch with a single to right, scoring Alvarez.

Unfortunately, the tie would be broken in the bottom of the 5th with a Luis Garcia two-run shot that brought home Ben Rice who had reached with a walk. The Garcia homer would chase Pecko from the game. Pecko's final stat line on his 24th birthday read: IP 4.1 with 5 earned on 5 hits. He'd allow 4 walks, while registering a lone strike out against Austin Wells . Bennett Sousa would come on in relief authoring a bounce back effort, going 1.2 innings, setting down each batter in order.

In the 6th inning, Jeremy Pena would answer and tie things up yet again. Yanier Diaz drew a walk and then Pena would launch his 15th HR of the year to center field. Suddenly, the Astros had new life, an energy surge racing through the dugout.

Steven Okert would come in the 7th, making his 65th appearance on the year. Unfortunately, he'd leave a series of breaking balls high in the zone and the Yankees would seize the lead. Trent Grisham would walk, Ben Rice singled and then a double by Luis Garcia would make it 6-5. Okert's night was done. Bryan Abreu would close out the 7th.

In the 8th, Yanier Diaz would take advantage of the short porch in left, hitting his second solo shot of the night. That would tie things up 6-6. Pena would then reach on a single and he'd score when Yordan Alvarez dropped a triple into the gap. It would be his first triple of the season and his 91st RBI. Isaac Paredes would single home Yordan, and it was 8-6 heading into the bottom of the 8th.

In the bottom of the 8th, Manager Joe Espada elected to stick with Abreu. He'd promptly give up a double to Spencer Jones, who would come around and score on a single by Jazz Chisholm . Jose Caballero would reach on a single, and then Josh Hader for just the second time this season would be asked to pitch more than one inning.

He was up to the challenge. Hader would record the next four outs and has not allowed a run in his last 15 appearances. Exhale! Astros win. There are now exactly 30 games left in the season. The Astros added an insurance run in the 9th. They'd finish the night with 14 hits and would score in six different innings.

Mike Burrows , who last pitched on July 6th (bounced early by the Nationals), will finally return to the mound Wednesday Night in the Bronx. First pitch set for 6:05pm CDT.

Yankees SS George Lombard Jr. has now committed a throwing error in four straight games.

articles.title: Yordan Alvarez hits go-ahead triple in 8th inning as Astros outlast Yankees 9-7
articles.summary: Yordan Alvarez went 3 for 5 and lined a go-ahead triple in the eighth inning off Brent Headrick as the Houston Astros beat the New York Yankees 9-7 on Tuesda...
articles.body:
NEW YORK (AP) — Yordan Alvarez went 3 for 5 and lined a go-ahead triple in the eighth inning off Brent Headrick as the Houston Astros beat the New York Yankees 9-7 on Tuesday night.

Yainer Diaz hit a pair of solo homers, including a tying shot to the short porch in right field off Headrick's fastball to start the eighth. After Jeremy Pena singled, Alvarez ripped a low-inside sinker to the warning track in right-center for a 7-6 lead.

Alvarez increased his major league-leading batting average to .323. The slugger had his seventh career triple and first since July 21, 2024.

Pena homered off Fernando Cruz in the sixth for a 5-all tie. Daulton Varsho had two RBI singles for the Astros, who won for the sixth time in 15 games after owner Jim Crane said manager Joe Espada will finish the season.

Isaac Paredes added an RBI single off Headrick (7-3), who has allowed five homers in 68 appearances. Headrick is second in the big leagues in appearances to Toronto lefty Mason Fluharty and permitted a run for only the 12th time.

Diaz tacked on an RBI single in the ninth off rookie Bradley Hanner as the Astros scored six runs against New York's bullpen.

Houston overcame a four-hit night by New York first baseman Luis García Jr. García hit an RBI double off Steven Okert that gave the Yankees a 6-5 lead and also launched a two-run homer in the fifth off rookie starter Ethan Packo.

It was García's third four-hit game this season and the eighth of his career.

Bryan Abreu (5-3) allowed an RBI single to Jazz Chisholm Jr. before finishing a double play against Austin Wells with a nice grab at first base. Josh Hader got four outs for his 19th save in 19 chances.

Cody Bellinger hit a three-run homer in the third that broke a 32-game homerless drought and gave the Yankees a 3-2 lead.

Packo allowed five runs and five hits in 4 1/3 innings on his 24th birthday.

New York starter Will Warren permitted three runs — two earned — and seven hits in five innings.

Astros RHP Peter Lambert (8-7, 3.68 ERA) pitches Wednesday night. The Yankees had not announced a scheduled starter.
